# H-2A Paper agent documentation

> Grounded technical context for coding agents working on the empirical pipeline.

Start with the repository `AGENTS.md`, then run `python scripts/agent_docs.py snapshot --scope <target-path>`.
The machine-readable instruction and reviewed-source bundle is [`/grounding-manifest.json`](/grounding-manifest.json).

## Declared high-risk assumptions

- `ACCESS-001` (critical, repository data access) — Non-public NASS data and custom tabulations are unavailable by user instruction. Use publicly released NASS data; the implemented county-level work requires no farm-level nonparticipant frame or institutional-access application.
- `AUTH-001` (critical, repository) — Executable code, runners, locks, and machine checks outrank prose when sources disagree.
- `GROUND-001` (critical, agent documentation) — A source-region digest can be accepted only after the linked documentation context changes.
- `GEO-001` (critical, shared pipeline) — Persistent geographic identifiers are strings and county FIPS uses the 2010 vintage, including 46102 to 46113 harmonization.
- `EMPLOYER-001` (critical, H-2A worksite-business linkage) — The supported employer unit is the v2 worksite business linked with FY2008--FY2026 (Q4 release) identity evidence (manual review of the FY2026 Q4 extension pending, declared as review status `pending`); the balanced tier is canonical, and alias-only individual masters are not counted as businesses.
- `PRED-001` (critical, prediction and shared panel) — The supported H-2A prediction is the static climate_norm_static_v1 model trained through 2011.
- `PANEL-001` (critical, shared panel) — The common baseline is a complete 2008--2025 county-year calendar with unique string county keys; sources that end earlier remain missing. The shared panel is design-neutral and excludes treatments, post indicators, design fixed effects, target clusters, and instruments.
- `OUTCOME-001` (critical, empirical designs) — The supported causal-outcome union contains thirteen outcomes, and each design's executable registry controls its subset, scaling, denominator, and sample rule.
- `DID-001` (critical, difference in differences) — The supported event study uses 2011 as its reference and clusters inference by CZ-by-AEWR-region.
- `IV-001` (critical, panel IV) — Panel IV retains the original moving-wage design with deterministic county entropy weights and source year t-1. All branch stages and tests are R. The fixed-wage revision, later exploratory exercises, simulated calibration draws, the wage-only instrument and the continuing control set were retired by explicit user instruction. estimation_spec.json is the sole model/outcome registry: two columns on the wage-plus-seasonal/composition instrument, without controls (column1) and with the committed BEA controls (column2, preferred). Estimation policy years are 2011--2023 because CAEMP25N ends in 2022; the instrument and the branch panel are still constructed through 2024. Stage04 recovers only the wage-plus-seasonal/composition distribution; the wage-only calibration and its z_wage_only_real field were retired with the wage-only columns. Preserve original donor support, prior behavior, twelve outcomes, reviewed business linkage, controls, equal weights, county/year FE and target-subregion CRV1. The farm-floor selection explicitly records the original all-domain Census source rows and refuses source-fingerprint drift; revising those choices is an empirical change. Recovered weights are not observed sampling errors; current FLS wage targets may induce mechanical relevance. The runner validates at stage09 and ends with the user-requested stage10 Kitagawa decomposition diagnostic, which uses recovered weights as-is, fixes donor wages at their 2008--2010 real mean on a balanced donor set, reports component variance shares only, and never replaces the instrument or selects a model, and with the user-requested stage11 QWI wage-granularity diagnostic, which multiplies the OEWS wage by an annual county QWI NAICS 111/112 factor in memory and recalibrates the weights on it, writes no calibration or instrument artifact, estimates no outcome equation and never selects a wage source; the OEWS proxy remains the only wage of the calibration and the instrument.
- `MC-001` (critical, Mundlak-Chamberlain) — The supported MC version-4.1 default is a bounded linear-history OLS registry with five primitive outcomes; requested positions and their derived rate are excluded without restricting the declared common sample; randomization and bootstrap inference are disabled, and the scalar continuous CCV-HC3 mixture is an explicitly experimental comparator rather than a Lean-proved exact reference law.
- `WELFARE-001` (critical, narrow welfare) — The narrow welfare branch (v2 scenario_bounds_grid) reports static partial-equilibrium certification-space producer-incidence bounds for an anticipated +$1/hr AEWR increase (real PPI-2012 and 2024 nominal, plus +-10% and Oct. 2, 2025 statutory cut comparisons) across a declared certified-hours elasticity bounds grid anchored to the complete FY2026 Q4 Track 1 statutory PPML hours 95% jackknife lower bound (eta = -0.5985, G = 46 states) and FY2026 Q4 R7 offered-wage pass-through sensitivity, applied to all 3,108 shared-panel counties in 2011--2025 with fail-closed SHA-256 and CSV parity checks; paid-hours incidence remains rho times every reported monetary result.
- `BORDER-001` (critical, AEWR-border bounded redesign) — The user-approved v7 border baseline extends policy years to 2011--2025 using the common 2008--2025 panel and retains all v5 benchmark model families and evaluates four declared local redesigns. New members satisfy frozen agricultural screens and surviving-edge one-ring locality; direct current-real-AEWR, certifications/fixed2011 employment and county/component-year FE remain. Fixed weights/history and region-disjoint matching are labeled sensitivities. Pair inference is retained alongside shared-endpoint/spatial size/power and region deletion evidence; the nonstatutory 2009 wage is excluded from new wage diagnostics and FE-only noise calibration never uses it. No significance-based selection or empirical-adequacy claim follows from completed code. The separate statewide_design.json registry (stages 12-13) declares the 2025-10-02 statewide-AEWR state-border design before any post-policy outcome is parsed; its power uses only pre-period FE-only scale and actual statewide rates.
- `AEWR-001` (critical, AEWR source extraction and shared-panel consumers) — Canonical 2009 AEWR is null; application means are quarantined in explicitly nonstatutory fields. Annual references retain 1990--2025 independently of validation coverage. Dated FLS and occupation/skill tables retain job-cohort and competing-floor limitations. Shared outcomes survive wage missingness; stage04 alone reconstructs the contaminated historical comparator. Frozen 2009 OEWS loadings remain a distinct source.
- `WORKSITE-001` (critical, H-2A disclosure dates, allocation calendar and point-geocoding producers) — Employment periods use source-owned, era-specific whole date pairs with explicit basis; job-order dates never supply employment periods. Start-only records can contribute start-year positions but not interval exposure. Application status counts share an intended-start cohort. Allocated certification position-days are capacity, not realized employment. Site dates and case fallback remain distinguishable; unreconciled cases are quarantined and county/month expansion conserves mass. Missing hours, unmatched counties and unacquired geocodes remain explicit. Outcome-weighted FLS references are timing diagnostics, and applicant locations do not supply a nonparticipant population.
- `REFORM-001` (critical, historical wage-reform investigation) — Historical wage-reform outputs are diagnostics, not a promoted causal elasticity. Cohort type and geography are fixed at baseline; absent certification is zero participation while wages stay missing. Observed 2009 application wages never assign statutory exposure, and old herder contracts are not grandfathered out of the wage increase.
- `CHAPTER-001` (critical, isolated chapter-direction exploration) — Offered wages and reference schedules do not establish applicable legal floors or realized earnings. Administrative exposure uses only recurring 2011/2012 cases; unavailable requested-start coverage stays unknown. The original earnings registry remains frozen as a historical record. The user-authorized November 14 interim amendment permits a declared 2025Q4/2026Q1 window with complete current/prior pairs; the original three-quarter estimate still requires full coverage and verified publication. Interim and later estimates are multiple outcome looks.
- `POLICY2025-001` (critical, 2025 policy-shift design) — Since the user's instruction of November 21, 2026 the baseline is the complete FY2026 H-2A disclosure (Q4 release): the wage window is the full fiscal year and the exposure table is rebuilt from that vintage; earlier specifications are not preserved and outcomes were inspected beforehand. The November 25, 2026 dated vintage update (history/vintage_update_2026_11_25.json) aligned state_real_minwages.parquet and county_year_panel.parquet to the unified A01 FRED minimum-wage producer, added an explicit !anyNA(r$ag_min) guard in 01_build_wages.R, and re-baselined only the 48 schedule_envelope_* reference-diagnostic rows in tests/fixtures/wage_estimates.csv (44->46 states in 2024--2025, 39->46 in 2026; max_abs_diff = 0.0 across all 135 earnings_pre, 46 earnings_interim, and 299 non-envelope wage rows). The first November 26, 2026 additive amendment (history/quantity_amendment_2026_11_26.json) added stage 11_estimate_quantity.R (79 Track 1 county quantity rows across 2,921 multi-state counties and 46 states, County + Former-Region x FY FE, state-deletion CV3J t(45) inference) while keeping all 22 source inputs and all 528 existing wage and earnings rows invariant; its complete FY2026 Q4 full-FY PPML certified-hours estimate (-0.078, 95% CI [-0.598, +0.443], MDE 0.72) anchors the separate code/welfare v2 bounds grid as a one-season lower bound rather than a tightly pinned point estimate. A second November 26, 2026 additive amendment (history/mechanisms_amendment_2026_11_26.json) added stage 11b_estimate_mechanisms.R (96 mechanism-heterogeneity rows across 5 panels with 12 Holm-adjusted primary hypotheses, min p_holm = 0.939, and matched FY2024--FY2025 placebos) plus code-generated manuscript tables and figures, expanding sources/input_vintage.json to 24 cached inputs while keeping all 607 pre-existing rows invariant (703 total validated rows, 356/356 validation checks, 52 published artifacts). The current earnings window is 2025Q4/2026Q1 with complete current/prior pairs; the original full-window release gate remains distinct. R7 filers are not worksite businesses, exact wage floors remain unresolved, and covered earnings do not identify domestic-worker wage rates. Every declared fit and failed deletion is retained with state jackknife inference; 2013 shutdown work stays outside this design.
- `BITE-001` (critical, full-panel FE-PPML bite design) — The standalone full-panel FE-PPML bite branch (code/designs/bite, scripts/run_bite.sh) remains outside scripts/run_all.sh and leaves shared C01/C02 and retained DiD untouched. It uses the balanced 3,108-county x 18-year (2008--2025) panel with canonical 2009 AEWR strictly NULL, freezes all exposures (E_p25, E_oews, all-real E_sf_log) strictly over 2008/2010, preserves 2023--2025 via predetermined 2008--2010 X_pre x Year controls, retains full-panel zeros via FE-PPML without excluding always-takers, and reports exact delete-one-cluster jackknife (CV3J) SEs alongside CRV1. Relative differential coefficients on E_c x ln(AEWR) are not aggregate AEWR elasticities, and the standalone 48-state ln(prevailing_ag_min_wage) domestic-floor margin is never translated into an AEWR elasticity.

## Grounding rule

A matching SHA-256 means the named source region has not changed since the linked page was reviewed. It does not independently prove the prose or empirical claim.
